caseno: Criminal Revision No. 1102(R) of 1995 with Criminal Appeal No. 396 of 1996
lawyer:
Kh. Gulzar Hossain, Advocate — For the Petitioner. 
Md. Altafur Rahman, Assistant Attorney-General— For the State
parties:
Rahmat Ali ----- Appellant-Petitioner
Vs.
State ----- Respondent
full_judgment:
This Rule on an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act was issued calling upon the Deputy Commissioner, Nilphamari to show cause as to why the delay of 1649 days in filing the appeal should not be condoned or such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. It appears that the appellant petitioner Rahmat Ali was tried in absentia along with 2 other co-accused’s on charge of murder under sections 302/34 of the Penal Code by the Sessions Judge, Nilphamari in Sessions Case No. 28 of 1989. After trial the learned Sessions Judge convicted the appellant petitioner with 2 others under sections 304 part (2)/34 of the Penal Code and sentenced them to suffer rigorous imprisonment for a period of 4 years each and to pay a fine of Taka 5000.00 in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 2 months more vide his judgment and order dated 4-11-1990. Against this judgment and order of conviction and sentence 2 other accused persons who were present in court filed an appeal being Criminal Appeal No. 1252 of 1990 which is pending for hearing. Thereafter this appellant-petitioner has preferred the present appeal against the above mentioned judgment and order of conviction and sentence with a delay of 1649 days and by filing a separate application under section 5 of the Limitation Act has prayed for condonation of this delay whereupon the present Rule was issued. 

 5. Mr. Gulzar Hossain submits that there is no material or any loth of evidence against this appellant petitioner in the whole case except his name in the First Information Report which is not a substantive evidence and, as such, the petitioner has merit in the appeal and in that view of the matter also the delay in filing the appeal needs be condoned and his appeal should be heard along with the other appeal No. 1252 of 1990 already filed by the co-accuseds of the case. The learned Advocate submits that the subject matter of both the appeals being the same both should be heard on merit. The petitioner having a merit in his appeal, his appeal should not be left out on the ground of limitation only. 

 6. From the facts and circumstances of the case as stated in the application under section 5 of the Limitation Act for condonation of the delay, it appears, that the appellant petitioner was absent in the trial on the ground that he was not aware of the case. It is not understood as to why the police could not arrest the petitioner. The petitioner's case that he did not see the notification in the newspaper and that no warrant of proclamation and attachment was served in the village address of the petitioner. All the above facts and circumstances as stated in paragraphs 3, 4 and 5 of the application deserve some consideration as exceptional circumstances preventing the petitioner from appearing in the case and from having any knowledge about the judgment passed against him.
